title: GE Foundations: Writing and Information Literacy
description: A first-year writing course that teaches academic writing, argument, revision, and finding and evaluating sources. Students write several papers for different audiences and purposes. Many universities require one such course of all students.
notes: OSU gen-ed category (GE-Writing). Students choose from an approved list.

title: GE Foundations: Social and Behavioral Sciences
description: A general education course on how individuals, groups, and societies behave, from a field such as psychology, sociology, economics, or political science. These courses introduce the field's research methods and main theories.
notes: OSU gen-ed category (GE-SBS). Students choose from an approved list.

title: GE Foundations: Race, Ethnicity and Gender Diversity
description: A general education course on how race, ethnicity, and gender shape people's experiences and social structures, often with a focus on the United States. Courses come from fields such as history, sociology, and ethnic or gender studies.
notes: OSU gen-ed category (GE-Diversity). Students choose from an approved list.

title: GE Foundations: Historical and Cultural Studies
description: A general education course that studies a past period, culture, or society through historical sources and methods. These courses help students explain how the past shapes the present and interpret historical evidence.
notes: OSU gen-ed category (GE-History). Students choose from an approved list.

title: GE Foundations: Literary, Visual and Performing Arts
description: A general education course in literature, visual art, film, music, theater, or dance. Students analyze and interpret creative works and sometimes make their own.
notes: OSU gen-ed category (GE-Lit/VPA). Students choose from an approved list.

title: GE Theme
description: An upper-level general education course in an interdisciplinary theme, such as citizenship, sustainability, or health and well-being. Theme courses ask students to connect ideas across fields and apply them to a broad question.
notes: OSU requires two 4-hour Themes, one in Citizenship for a Diverse and Just World. Both schedule rows share this description.

title: Math or Science Elective
description: An additional mathematics or natural science course chosen from a list approved by the program. Typical choices include further calculus or differential equations, a second physics course, chemistry, or biology.
notes: OSU: 8 hours from an approved list.

title: Technical Elective
description: An advanced computer science course chosen by the student, sometimes with a limited number of approved courses from related fields. Common options cover areas such as machine learning, security, graphics, networking, and software engineering. Technical electives let students go deeper in an area of interest.
notes: OSU: 17 hours, at least 9 in CSE at the 3000 level or higher.

title: CSE 390X (CSE 3901 or CSE 3902 or CSE 3903)
description: A team software project course in which students design, build, and document a sizable system. Students choose the kind of system: web applications, interactive systems such as games, or system software. These courses emphasize teamwork, design, testing, and written documentation.
notes: Choice slot. Official descriptions of each option are in data/raw/osu/courses/.

title: CSE 32X1 (CSE 3231 or CSE 3241)
description: A choice between a software engineering course (requirements, design, testing, project management, and team process) and a database course (the relational model, SQL, database design, and query processing).
notes: Choice slot. Official descriptions of each option are in data/raw/osu/courses/.

title: CSE 34X1 (CSE 3421 or CSE 3461)
description: A choice between a computer architecture course (instruction sets, processor design, pipelining, and memory hierarchy) and a computer networking course (network layers, the Internet protocols, routing, and network applications).
notes: Choice slot. Official descriptions of each option are in data/raw/osu/courses/.

title: CSE 35X1 (CSE 3521 or CSE 3541)
description: A choice between an introductory artificial intelligence course (search, knowledge representation, reasoning, and basic machine learning) and an introductory computer graphics or game and animation course (rendering, transformations, and interactive animation).
notes: Choice slot. Official descriptions of each option are in data/raw/osu/courses/.

title: CSE 591X (CSE 5911 or CSE 5912 or CSE 5913 or CSE 5914 or CSE 5915)
description: A senior capstone design course in which student teams carry out a substantial project, usually for an outside or faculty client. Students choose the area, such as software applications, games, animation, knowledge-based systems, or information systems. Capstones emphasize design, teamwork, communication, and professional practice.
notes: Choice slot. Official descriptions of the options offered in 2026-27 are in data/raw/osu/courses/ (CSE 5913 was not offered).
